subject: Maths
title: Plotting straight-line graphs
subtitle: Straight-Line Graphs · GCSE Maths
learning_objective: I can plot straight-line graphs by generating a table of values and drawing the line.

key_vocab.definition: To plot a straight line, substitute values of x into the equation to find corresponding y-values. Plot these coordinate pairs and join with a ruler.

sections.title: Learning Objective
sections.content: I can plot straight-line graphs by generating a table of values and drawing the line.

sections.title: Key Words
sections.content: plot a straight line -- To plot a straight line, substitute values of x into the equation to find corresponding y-values. Plot these coordinate pairs and join with a ruler.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
Substitute at least three x-values into the equation. Plot the (x, y) pairs and join with a straight line.
x = 0 ⇒ y = c, x = 1 ⇒ y = m + c
Start with x = 0 to find the y-intercept

Key examples:
  ✓ y = 2x + 1: when x = 0, y = 1; when x = 2, y = 5  (substitute x values)
  ✓ Use x = 0, 1, 2, 3 to make a table of values  (systematic approach)
  ✓ Three collinear points confirms the line  (error check)
  ✗ Only need one point to draw a line  (need at least two)
  ✗ Join the points freehand  (always use a ruler)

sections.title: Worked Example
sections.content:
Example 1 – table of values
  Complete a table for y = 3x - 1 with x = 0, 1, 2, 3.
  x = 0: y = -1; x = 1: y = 2
  x = 2: y = 5; x = 3: y = 8
  Points: (0,-1), (1,2), (2,5), (3,8)
  y values: -1, 2, 5, 8
  (Substitute each x-value into the equation.)

Example 2 – using intercepts
  Plot y = 2x - 4 using x and y intercepts.
  y-intercept: x = 0, y = -4 gives (0, -4)
  x-intercept: y = 0, 2x = 4, x = 2 gives (2, 0)
  Plot (0, -4) and (2, 0) and join
  Line through (0, -4) and (2, 0)
  (Intercepts give two quick points without a full table.)

sections.title: Completing tables
sections.content:
Complete the table of values for x = 0, 1, 2, 3.

(a) y = 2x + 3
(b) y = x - 2
(c) y = 4x - 1
(d) y = -2x + 5

sections.title: Finding intercepts
sections.content:
Find the x-intercept and y-intercept.

(a) y = 3x - 6
(b) y = -2x + 8
(c) y = x + 4
(d) y = 5x - 10

sections.title: Negative and fractional gradients
sections.content:
Complete values for x = -2, 0, 2, 4.

(a) y = -3x + 2
(b) y = &frac{1}{2}x + 3
(c) y = -&frac{1}{2}x + 4
(d) y = &frac{3}{2}x - 1

sections.title: Identifying equations from points
sections.content:
Which equation matches the points given?

(a) (0, 2) and (1, 5)
(b) (0, -1) and (2, 3)
(c) (0, 4) and (2, 0)
(d) (0, 0) and (3, 6)

sections.title: Mixed plotting problems
sections.content:
Solve each problem.

(a) y = x + 3. Value of y when x = -2?
(b) y = 2x - 5. When does y = 0?
(c) Lines y = x + 1 and y = 3x - 3. Where do they meet?
(d) y = -x + 6. Value of x when y = 2?
(e) y = 4x - 8. Give 3 points on this line.

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
✓ You need at least two points to draw a straight line
✗ You only need one point to plot a line
✓ The y-intercept is found by setting x = 0
✓ For y = &frac{1}{2}x + 1, when x = 1, y = 1.5
✗ All straight lines pass through the origin

teacher_sections.title: Teacher Key & Mark Scheme
teacher_sections.content:
Award marks for correct working and final answers.

Completing tables:
  (a) y = 3, 5, 7, 9
  (b) y = -2, -1, 0, 1
  (c) y = -1, 3, 7, 11
  (d) y = 5, 3, 1, -1

Finding intercepts:
  (a) y-int (0, -6), x-int (2, 0)
  (b) y-int (0, 8), x-int (4, 0)
  (c) y-int (0, 4), x-int (-4, 0)
  (d) y-int (0, -10), x-int (2, 0)

Negative and fractional gradients:
  (a) y = 8, 2, -4, -10
  (b) y = 2, 3, 4, 5
  (c) y = 5, 4, 3, 2
  (d) y = -4, -1, 2, 5

Identifying equations from points:
  (a) y = 3x + 2
  (b) y = 2x - 1
  (c) y = -2x + 4
  (d) y = 2x

Mixed plotting problems:
  (a) y = 1
  (b) x = 2.5
  (c) (2, 3)
  (d) x = 4
  (e) (0,-8), (2,0), (3,4)
